properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 12 at 5:59PM EST until November 12 at 10:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
FFWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Monmouth County in central New Jersey...
Northeastern Ocean County in southern New Jersey...

* Until 1000 PM EST.

* At 559 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Long Branch, Asbury Park, Tinton Falls, Manasquan, Point Pleasant
Beach, Allenwood, Collingwood Park, Elberon, Ramtown, Point
Pleasant, Eatontown and West Long Branch.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 2:58PM PST until November 14 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to
35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored
breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large
breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls,
inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from
midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49
PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the
Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea
walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of

property.

infrastructure.

infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 12 at 11:49AM PST until November 13 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to
15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning,
dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous
rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain
far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through
Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be
west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely
at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.description:

higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night.

elevations of 2,500 feet, mainly a dusting to half inch on grassy and
elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow accumulations

snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in the 20s could
yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of Highway 160
near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on Friday night.
properties.instruction:

weather conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Tillamook County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 10:22AM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding
expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous
surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Tillamook County Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon to 4 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from noon Friday to noon
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Garibaldi tidal gauge is forecast to reach approximately
10.5 ft during high tide Friday afternoon. This typically
results in flooding over Burton-Fraser Rd. along the Tillamook
River.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

properties.description:
Recent dry conditions have made outdoor burning increasingly
hazardous. Conditions are such that a spark from equipment, the
heat from a catalytic converter, or any heat source could start a
grass or brush fire. The combination of dry fine fuels, such as
grass, and low relative humidity have resulted in continued fire
danger across the region.

this afternoon, creating high fire danger given the dry and breezy
conditions.

present time. Fires place local forestry agencies, fire
departments, and other fire control agencies in life threatening
situations, and can endanger communities. Please use caution and
help prevent forest and grass fires.

local restrictions should be followed.
